title: The 10 Best Electric Pressure Washers
subtitle: Corded electric pressure washers for cars, decks, siding and driveways, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: An electric pressure washer plugs into the wall: no gas, no oil, and it starts with a button. We ranked 10 best-sellers from Westinghouse, Greenworks, Sun Joe, Kärcher, CRAFTSMAN and A-iPower on rating, review volume and features (independently rated performance, an onboard soap tank, a 25-foot or longer hose and an induction or brushless motor). Compare rated PSI and GPM, not the bigger max numbers on the box.

changelog.note: Page published with 10 ranked picks and 1 tool to avoid.

products.name: Westinghouse ePX3500 Electric Pressure Washer, 2500 Max PSI 1.76 Max GPM, Anti-Tipping, Onboard Soap Tank, Steel Wand, 5 Nozzles
products.verdict: The best-selling pressure washer here by far: 2,000 rated PSI, a 25-foot hose, a 20 oz onboard soap tank and five quick-connect nozzles in a 19 lb body that won't tip over.
products.best_for: Most homes: cars, patio furniture, siding, fences and small decks.
products.skip_if: You clean big driveways often; the 3,000 PSI models are faster.
pros: 25 ft hose and onboard soap tank

products.name: Westinghouse WPX3000e Electric Pressure Washer, 3000 Max PSI 1.76 Max GPM, Induction Motor, Onboard Soap Tank, 5 Nozzles

specs.extras: 35 ft GFCI cord, 10 in never-flat wheels, steel frame

products.verdict: A step up to an induction motor (quieter and longer-lived than the usual universal motor), 2,600 rated PSI, a steel frame with 10-inch never-flat wheels and a 35-foot GFCI cord.
products.best_for: Driveways, decks and regular heavy use where motor life matters.
products.skip_if: You need to store it in a small space; it's a full cart-style washer.
pros: Steel frame, big wheels, 35 ft cord

products.name: Westinghouse ePX3100 Electric Pressure Washer, 2300 Max PSI 1.76 Max GPM, Anti-Tipping, Onboard Soap Tank, 5 Nozzles
products.verdict: The ePX3500's slightly smaller sibling, with the same 25-foot hose, soap tank and compact body at 1,900 rated PSI.
products.best_for: Cars, bikes, grills and patio furniture on a tighter budget.
products.skip_if: You can stretch to the ePX3500 for 100 more rated PSI.

products.name: Greenworks 3000 PSI (2.0 GPM Max) Brushless Electric Pressure Washer
products.verdict: A 14-amp brushless washer whose 3,000 PSI and 2.0 GPM figures were tested by an independent lab, according to the listing. It has a metal gun and a 25-foot kink-resistant hose.
products.best_for: Heavy cleaning like driveways and concrete where you want honest, tested numbers.
products.skip_if: You want an onboard soap tank; it uses an applicator instead.

products.name: Westinghouse WPX3400e Electric Pressure Washer, 3400 Max PSI 2.0 Max GPM, Brushless Motor, Onboard Soap Tank, 5 Nozzles

specs.extras: 35 ft GFCI cord, 10 in wheels, steel frame

products.verdict: Westinghouse's strongest electric here: a brushless motor with 3,000 rated PSI, a steel frame, big never-flat wheels and an onboard soap tank.
products.best_for: Big driveways, decks and siding where you want the most pressure from an outlet.
products.skip_if: You're on a budget; the ePX3500 does most homeowner jobs for less than half the price.

products.name: Sun Joe SPX3000 Electric Pressure Washer, 2500 Max PSI

specs.extras: Two 0.9 L detergent tanks, 5 tips, 34 in steel lance

products.verdict: The most-reviewed pressure washer here by far, with 64,682 reviews. It has two onboard detergent tanks, five tips and a 34-inch stainless lance.
products.best_for: Homeowners who want the most proven electric washer and two soap tanks.
products.skip_if: You want a longer reach; the hose is 20 feet.

products.name: Greenworks 2100 PSI (1.2 GPM) Electric Pressure Washer

specs.extras: 35 ft GFCI cord, turbo nozzle, push-button start

products.verdict: A medium-duty Greenworks with 2,100 PSI, a 35-foot GFCI cord, push-button start and a turbo nozzle. The bullets say 20-foot hose; the spec table says 25.
products.best_for: Fences, decks and vehicles on a mid budget.
products.skip_if: You want a soap tank; it comes with an applicator instead.

products.name: Kärcher K1700 Electric Pressure Washer, CETA Certified, 3 Spray Nozzles, Detergent Tank, 1.2 GPM

specs.extras: 0.5 gal detergent tank, foot switch, never-flat wheels

products.verdict: A light-duty Kärcher with CETA-certified 1,700 PSI, an on/off foot switch so you don't have to bend down, and a half-gallon detergent tank.
products.best_for: Cars, patio furniture and light cleaning from a brand that publishes tested numbers.
products.skip_if: You need to strip a deck or driveway; 1,700 PSI is light-duty.

products.name: CRAFTSMAN Electric Pressure Washer, 1700 PSI, 1.2 GPM, Cold Water
products.verdict: A compact CRAFTSMAN for cars and patios, with onboard storage for the nozzles, hose, cord and wand and a 20-foot kink-resistant hose.
products.best_for: Car washing and light patio cleaning in a small garage.
products.skip_if: You want more power; most others here have more PSI for similar money.

products.name: A-iPower Electric Pressure Washer 2800 Max PSI 1.7 Max GPM
products.verdict: A budget washer that lists both its max and rated numbers honestly: 2,000 rated PSI and 1.2 rated GPM, a 25-foot hose, a 35-foot cord and five nozzles.
products.best_for: A budget all-rounder with a long hose and cord.
products.skip_if: You want a known brand's service network.

avoid.name: Electric Pressure Washer 4500PSI 2.8 GPM with Anti-Tipping Technology
avoid.flag: 4,500 PSI at 2.8 GPM from a wall outlet
avoid.verdict: It claims 4,500 PSI and 2.8 GPM from an electric motor on a household outlet, numbers you normally see on large gas washers.
reasons: 4,500 PSI x 2.8 GPM is 12,600 'cleaning units', more than double the Greenworks 3000 PSI/2.0 GPM unit here, whose 14-amp brushless motor's figures are independently tested.
A standard 15-amp, 120V outlet supplies about 1,800 watts, which can't produce that much pressure and flow together. The listing gives no motor rating or amps to explain it.
It ships with a 20-foot power cord, shorter than the 35-foot GFCI cords on the Westinghouse, Greenworks and A-iPower washers.

buyers_guide.a: Max PSI is a brief peak at the nozzle; rated PSI is what the washer holds while you clean. Westinghouse and A-iPower list both; use the rated number to compare. Brands that are PWMA- or CETA-certified, or lab-tested like the Greenworks 3000, publish numbers that were checked independently.

buyers_guide.q: How much PSI do I need?
buyers_guide.a: 1,500 to 2,000 PSI handles cars, bikes and patio furniture. 2,000 to 2,600 PSI is right for siding, fences and decks. For concrete driveways and stains, look at 3,000 PSI models like the Greenworks or Westinghouse WPX3400e.
GPM is how much water you move, and it decides how fast you rinse. Multiply PSI by GPM for 'cleaning units': a 2,000 PSI, 1.2 GPM washer makes 2,400; a 3,000 PSI, 2.0 GPM washer makes 6,000.
Most cheap electrics use a universal motor that's loud and wears out. Induction and brushless motors, like those in the Westinghouse WPX models and Greenworks 3000, run quieter and last longer.

buyers_guide.q: Can I use an extension cord?
buyers_guide.a: Manufacturers generally say to plug directly into a GFCI outlet and add hose length instead of cord length. A long, thin extension cord drops voltage and can overheat the motor.
